Knowledge-base entry for 'Bacterial_Blight':
────────────────────────────────────────
Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions surrounded by a yellow halo; as disease progresses, lesions often grow together to produce large, irregularly shaped dead areas.. Centers of older lesions frequently fall out, causing leaves to appear tattered; symptoms usually begin in the upper canopy on young leaves.. Septoria brown spot, Bacterial pustule, Downy mildew, Soybean rust, Soybean vein necrosis, Insect and mite Injury

Knowledge-base entry for 'Diaporthe':
────────────────────────────────────────
For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Mature plants with stem canker can exhibit irregular, thin black lines or 'zone' lines on the interior of lower stems; black specks (pycnidia) appear in linear rows on stems for pod and stem blight.. Phytophthora, Sudden death syndrome, White Mold, Anthracnose, Brown Stem Rot, Charcoal Rot, Herbicide injury, Fungicide injury, Late season frost damage, Lightning damage
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes, girdling the stem; as disease progresses, damping off, stunting, yellowing, and brown lesions on lower stem can occur.. Diaporthe complex (stem canker), Fusarium root rot and wilt, Pythium seedling blight and root rot, Rhizoctonia seedling blight and root rot, Sudden death syndrome, White mold, Anthracnose stem blight, Brown stem rot, Charcoal rot, Herbicide injury, Early season frost damage, Insect and mite injury
────────────────────────────────────────

Phomopsis-infected seeds are cracked and shriveled and often covered with chalky, white mold. Infected seedlings have reddish-brown, pinpoint lesions on the cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line..
